newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African industrials end weak on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: S.African industrials end weak on profit-taking.

text.p: South African shares finished well down after directionless trade on Thursday as profit-taking and some negativity from disappointing results knocked prices, dealers said.
Golds lso ended weaker on the back of a dull bullion price, which failed to hold the gains the yellow metal made earlier this week.
The industrial index closed down 53.3 points at 8,440.6, and the gold index down 15.4 points at 1,254.7 and the all-share down 41.4 points at 7,173.1.
Some key industrial companies continued to report disappointing results on Thursday and dealers said this was unseating the market's sentiment further.
Dealers said the day's volumes were moderate with 772 million rand worth of shares exchanging hands at the close.
They said among stocks with rekindled interest on the market were New Africa Investment (Nail), Driefontein and Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd (GFSA).

Nail, the black empowerment group headed by former African National Congress secretary-general Cyril Ramaphosa, said on Thursday it planned to buy a stake in Gold Fields, the world's third largest gold producer.
It said the buy would give it an effective 17.2 percent stake in the mining house.
Nail said it was also in talks with Driefontein Consolidated Ltd which holds a 40 percent stake in Gold Fields, through its shareholding in Asteroid Ltd.
Gold Fields finished up 825 cents at 118.00 rand, Driefontein up 85 cents at 41.60 rand and Nail up 35 cents at 425 cents.
Dealers expected Friday's trade to be dreary and awaited no cue from the Dow as Wall Street was busy digesting a slew of U.S. economic data giving ambigious interest rate clues.
